From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: High rate of 504s/429s on checkout - impacting production

On investigation:
- We see a sudden surge in prefix cache evictions for CycloTech's tenant starting 09:08 UTC. Eviction rate jumped ~18x.
- Batching subsystem is holding large request groups while waiting for KV cache priming, causing head-of-line blocking — queues back up and timeouts follow.
- Retry storm: client retries that observe 504/429 are re-entering the request stream and amplifying the queueing.

Proposed immediate mitigations (deployable in ~20-35 minutes):
1) Disable prefix/KV caching for CycloTech tenant (fast toggle) to stop eviction churn.
2) Apply short-term conservative per-tenant rate limits and increase per-request scheduling priority for checkout routes.
3) Adjust batching window to 10ms and cap max batch size to reduce head-of-line waits.

Im attaching a small heap_profile and the eviction histogram. If agreed, Ill push the toggle and schedule a hotfix.

Attachments referenced: heap_profile_20270804.txt

— Monica
SRE, Redwood Inference

- Immediate: disable prefix cache for CycloTech + apply per-tenant throttles (now).
- Hotfix: batching scheduler patch to avoid waiting for cache priming; deploy to canary in 30m, global in 2h if green.
- Fallback: route CycloTech to a compatible model variant on less loaded pools if latency doesn't improve within 45m.

Business ask: Rachel, can you check with the customer re: credits? This will require an exec note if we need to offer a meaningful SLA credit.

From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@cyclotech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-06T18:04:00Z
Subject: Resolution and next steps — CycloTech outage 2027-08-04

Daniel —

Summary and timeline:
- 09:08 UTC (08-04): prefix cache eviction spike observed; batching waits for cache priming leading to queue blocking and timeouts.
- 09:30 UTC: we disabled tenant prefix cache and applied per-tenant rate limits. Immediate error-rate reduction observed; 504s dropped from ~12% to <1% over 15 minutes.
- 10:10 UTC: batching scheduler patch deployed to canary, rolled to production at 10:40 after verification.
- 12:00 UTC: traffic normalized; we continued to monitor for 48 hours.

Root cause: an interaction between recent batching optimizer (v1.14) and heavy small-request traffic from the tenant that caused repeated cache-priming eviction cycles. This escalated into client retry amplification.

Action items we completed:
- Deployed scheduler fix to prevent batches waiting on cache priming.
- Added tenant isolation thresholds and an automatic cache-disable heuristic on eviction spikes.
- Implemented a temporary adaptive rate-limit for checkout endpoints and updated the runbook.

Request for follow-up meeting: wed like 30 minutes to review the RCA and discuss SLA credit. Proposed slots: Tue 2027-08-09 16:00 or Wed 2027-08-10 10:00 (UTC).

Attachments: post-incident-runbook-0806.pdf

Again, sorry for the disruption — were treating this as P1 and have an internal action tracker (INFR-9123). We will provide a full written post-mortem with timelines in the next 72 hours.
